places.near: Trailhead is on Sans Souci Road opposite Copolia Lodge, ~15 min taxi from Victoria; agree a pickup time as taxis do not wait
places.notes: Fee/hours per Seychelles News Agency + SPGA trail information.
places.famousFor: Mahe's most rewarding short hike — a granite dome at 497 m with a 360-degree view over Victoria, Eden Island and the Sainte Anne marine park, plus pitcher plants near the top
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.8 ★ (882) · Open 08:00-16:00; entry about SCR 100 for non-residents over 12, card payment only (no cash). 1.4-1.6 km each way, 45-90 min up, moderate with steep granite steps and boulder scrambles. Start by 08:00 before the heat; the last slabs are slippery after rain — not for the 5-year-old · Location needs verification · Kids: Best 9+ (steep 1-1.5h climb)

places.name: Curieuse Island Giant Tortoises
places.near: Boat excursion from Anse Volbert or Baie Sainte Anne on Praslin, ~20-30 min crossing; almost always sold combined with the St Pierre snorkel stop
places.notes: Fees/tour prices per curieuseislandexcursions.com and GetYourGuide Praslin listings.
places.famousFor: Free-roaming Aldabra giant tortoises, a mangrove boardwalk, the old leper-colony Doctor's House and the only coco de mer forest outside Praslin
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.8 ★ (242) · Marine-park/island entry about SCR 300 pp for over-12s, card only (bring the card, cash is refused). Typical tours: half day about EUR 75 adult, full day about EUR 95 with Creole BBQ; children 5-11 usually half price, under-5s free. Full-day boats run roughly 09:00-16:00. Tortoises take leaves from the hand — the highlight for the younger kids · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — flat mangrove boardwalk

places.name: Moyenne Island
places.area: Mahe — Sainte Anne Marine National Park
places.near: Landing on a Sainte Anne marine-park boat trip from Eden Island Marina, Mahe; no scheduled public boats
places.notes: Landing-fee and tour inclusion per Sainte Anne marine-park tour operators.
places.famousFor: The one-man island of Brendon Grimshaw — a tiny national park with tame giant tortoises, two pirate graves and a jungle path he cut by hand
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.8 ★ (180) · Landing fee about EUR 12 pp paid on the island, usually not included in the tour price. The circuit walk takes 45 min in flip-flops; the tortoise feeding area is right by the landing beach. The pirate-treasure story is a hit with 9-15 year olds · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — 45-min flat island loop
places.address: Moyenne Island, Sainte Anne Marine National Park, Seychelles

places.name: Grand Anse & Anse Cocos
places.near: Cycle ~25 min across La Digue from La Passe to Grand Anse, then walk 20 min over the headland to Petite Anse and a further 20 min to Anse Cocos
places.notes: Rip-current warnings per La Digue guides and Expedia/Tripadvisor beach notes.
places.famousFor: La Digue's wild east-coast trio — Grand Anse, Petite Anse and the sheltered natural pool at Anse Cocos, reached by bike then a coastal footpath
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.8 ★ (169) · Free. Grand Anse and Petite Anse have powerful rip currents and no lifeguards — do not let children swim, especially May-Oct. Only the rock-protected pool at the north end of Anse Cocos is safe on a calm day. No shops after Grand Anse: carry water, and start early to avoid midday heat · Location needs verification · Kids: Look only — rip currents; 11+ walk

places.name: Anse Intendance
places.near: South Mahe past Takamaka; ~45 min drive from Victoria, then a steep side road to the public car park by Banyan Tree
places.notes: Current/season warnings per SeyVillas beach guide + Seychelles beach-safety guides.
places.famousFor: Wild, reefless south-coast bay with big surf, palm-fringed dunes and turtle tracks — the most cinematic beach on Mahe
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.7 ★ (1,029) · Free, no lifeguards, drownings have occurred. A rip forms near the southern rocks; the shore break is heaviest May-Oct (south-east monsoon) when swimming should be avoided entirely. Calmest Apr-May and Oct-Nov. Treat it as a walking/photo beach with the 5- and 9-year-olds and respect red flags · Location needs verification · Kids: Teens/adults — strong rip currents

places.name: Sainte Anne Marine National Park Glass-Bottom Boat
places.near: Boats leave Eden Island Marina, ~10 min from the airport and ~15 min from Victoria; the park lies 15-20 min offshore
places.notes: Prices/schedule per SeyVillas and SeyWorld St Anne glass-bottom tour listings.
places.famousFor: Seychelles' first marine park (1973) — coral gardens viewed dry through the hull, fish feeding, snorkelling and a beach BBQ on a small island
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.7 ★ (639) · Full day roughly 09:30-16:00, around EUR 90 pp with BBQ lunch; the Moyenne Island landing fee (about EUR 12 pp) is usually paid separately on the day. Dolphin Nemo and Teddy's are the long-established operators. Book a private boat for a family of 7 if you want your own schedule; the glass hull means non-swimmers still see the reef · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — great for a 5-yr-old

places.name: Anse Volbert (Cote d'Or)
places.near: North coast of Praslin, ~15 min from Baie Sainte Anne jetty by taxi or hire car; the main Praslin bus route stops along the beach road
places.notes: General Praslin beach and operator information from Praslin travel guides.
places.famousFor: Praslin's long, sheltered family bay with a swim-out islet (Chauve Souris) and the island's main strip of cafes, shops and boat operators
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.7 ★ (42) · Free; calm, shallow and safe for small children — the best base beach on Praslin. Kayaks, pedalos and glass-bottom boats hire on the sand; most Curieuse/St Pierre boats leave from here. Plenty of shade under takamaka trees and easy access to lunch · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — shallow and sheltered
places.address: Anse Volbert, Cote d'Or, Praslin, Seychelles

places.name: The Knysna Pirate Ship
places.near: Departs the Knysna Waterfront, 20 Waterfront Drive, Knysna, on the Garden Route
places.order: The ~90-min cruise to the Knysna Heads with the costumed captain and crew; kids' pirate training, sword fights and treasure hunts
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Family pirate-ship lagoon cruise on the Knysna Lagoon aboard the 'Black Pearl' (Zamani), a 1968 Seychelles-built vessel
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.7 ★ (34) · Geared to families and kids' parties; you may spot seals or dolphins near the Heads. Kids' tickets include a pirate pack (ages 2-12). · Location needs verification

places.name: Wooden Shoe Workshop of Zaanse Schans
places.near: At the Zaanse Schans heritage village in Zaandam, north of Amsterdam
places.order: Watch a clog-carving demonstration and see the Swarovski-crystal 'diamond clog'
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Family-run clog workshop and museum at Zaanse Schans with live wooden-shoe making demonstrations and one of the Netherlands' finest antique clog collections
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.6 ★ (9,501) · Free admission; short frequent demonstrations; open daily (8:00-18:00 in summer) · Location needs verification

places.name: Anse Source d'Argent
places.near: Cat Cocos ferry Mahe-Praslin-La Digue (Mahe-La Digue ~1h45, from about EUR 68 adult / EUR 39 child one-way), then bike or ox-cart/taxi 10 min south to L'Union Estate; the beach is entered only through the estate gate
places.notes: Fees/access per lunionestate.com and 2026 visitor reports; coordinates from Wikipedia.
places.famousFor: The most photographed beach on earth: sculpted pink-granite boulders, powder sand and a shin-deep turquoise lagoon protected by a reef
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.6 ★ (2,380) · Entry is via L'Union Estate ticket (about SCR 150-300 pp, valid all day, re-entry allowed); water is very shallow — at low tide it is more wading pool than swimming; keep walking 10-15 min past the first bay for the emptiest boulder coves; late afternoon light is the best and the crowds thin after 15:30 · Kids: All ages — shallow, calm lagoon

places.name: Fond Ferdinand Nature Reserve
places.near: South-east Praslin near Anse Marie-Louise; ~15 min drive from Baie Sainte Anne jetty
places.notes: Fee/tour times per SeyVillas + Fond Ferdinand visitor guides (prices vary by source).
places.famousFor: The quieter alternative to Vallee de Mai: a guided climb through coco de mer forest to a granite outcrop overlooking Baie Sainte Anne, La Digue and the sister islands
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.6 ★ (1,174) · Entry about SCR 130-300 pp and a personal guide is included and compulsory; tours leave through the morning (09:30 and 11:30 are the usual slots) and stop around 13:00. Allow 2-3 hours, steep in places — good shoes, hats and water. Better parrot and view odds than Vallee de Mai and far fewer people · Location needs verification · Kids: 9+ — 2h uphill guided walk
places.address: Fond Ferdinand, Anse Marie-Louise, Praslin, Seychelles

places.name: Petite Anse (Four Seasons Beach)
places.near: Baie Lazare, south-west Mahe, ~30 min from the airport; park outside the Four Seasons gate, register at security for a wristband, then walk 10-15 min down the hill (staff sometimes give a buggy lift)
places.notes: Access/wristband procedure per Tripadvisor Petite Anse reviews and beach guides.
places.famousFor: A perfect scoop of white sand below the Four Seasons hillside — public beach, private-resort feel
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.6 ★ (1,017) · Beach is public and free but access crosses the resort — arrive early, parking is limited and there are no public sunbeds. Swimming is lovely on calm days and rough with south-east swell. Only food is the resort restaurant (expensive, reservation needed); bring water and snacks for the kids · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages on calm days; check swell
places.address: Petite Anse, Baie Lazare, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Anse Soleil
places.near: Turn off the Baie Lazare road onto the steep, narrow Anse Soleil track (small cars only; taxis will drop you); ~35 min from the airport
places.notes: Access and size details from Mahe beach guides (Sandee, seychelles.cc).
places.famousFor: A pocket-sized hidden cove reached down a rough lane — locals' pick for sunset and a beach-shack lunch
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.6 ★ (144) · Free; about 200 m of sand so it fills quickly — go before 10:00 or after 15:00. Snorkelling around the right-hand rocks. The access road is potholed and steep; a 7-seater will struggle, consider two taxis. Simple Creole cafe at the beach · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — small cove, easy water
places.address: Anse Soleil, Baie Lazare, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Beau Vallon Beach
places.near: ~25-30 min drive from Seychelles International Airport over the Bel Air pass; frequent SPTC public buses from Victoria (about SCR 12)
places.notes: Watersports/atmosphere per Tripadvisor + Inside Seychelles Beau Vallon guides.
places.famousFor: Mahe's long, wide swimming beach — the island's watersports and sunset hub, with cafes, dive centres and a Wednesday/Saturday evening food bazar
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.5 ★ (1,120) · Free; the only Mahe beach with lifeguards in season and full facilities. Calm Nov-Apr; May-Oct the south-east trades bring chop and seaweed. Parasailing, banana boat, kayaks, jet-ski and glass-bottom boats operate from the sand — agree the price before boarding. Evening bazar with grilled fish and Creole snacks is a good family dinner · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — the easiest family beach

places.name: Anse Major Trail
places.area: Mahe — Bel Ombre, Morne Seychellois NP
places.near: Start at the end of the road in Bel Ombre, ~3 km past Beau Vallon; taxi or bus to the Danzil terminus then walk. Boat option: the small taxi-boat runs roughly hourly back to Bel Ombre marina or Beau Vallon for about SCR 150 pp
places.notes: Duration and taxi-boat fare per Savoy Resort blog + Anse Major hiking guides.
places.famousFor: A coastal cliff path through glacis granite and endemic scrub to Anse Major, a road-free beach with no buildings at all
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.5 ★ (99) · Free; 4.2 km return, 30-60 min each way, mostly flat with a descent at the end and almost no shade — go early and carry water. Best family plan: walk in, swim, ride the boat back. Sea can be rough May-Oct; no facilities, no shop, take everything with you · Location needs verification · Kids: Fine from 5 with breaks; boat back

places.name: Cousin Island Special Reserve
places.near: Boat tour from Praslin (Anse Volbert or Baie Sainte Anne), often combined with Curieuse; visitors transfer to the reserve's own boats for a surf landing on the beach — there is no jetty
places.notes: Days, hours and fees per Nature Seychelles' official Visit Cousin Island page.
places.famousFor: A rescued seabird island run by Nature Seychelles — thousands of nesting terns and noddies, endemic warblers and magpie-robins, and one of the region's key hawksbill turtle beaches
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.4 ★ (41) · Open Monday-Friday only, roughly 09:45-12:30, closed weekends and public holidays. Entry about SCR 600 for non-residents, free for under-12s. Guided walk with a warden is compulsory (about 1 hour, flat). Expect to get feet and shorts wet at the landing — dry bag recommended · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages; wet beach landing

places.name: Vallee de Mai Nature Reserve (UNESCO)
places.area: Praslin — Fond B'Offay / centre of island
places.near: Centre of Praslin on the Vallee de Mai cross-island road; ~15 min taxi from Baie Sainte Anne jetty or Anse Volbert, Praslin buses stop at the gate
places.notes: Hours/fee per SIF and Praslin visitor guides 2026; coordinates from Wikipedia.
places.famousFor: UNESCO World Heritage prehistoric palm forest — about 5,000 coco de mer palms bearing the largest seed in the plant kingdom (30-40 kg), plus the endemic black parrot
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.3 ★ (1,942) · Open daily 08:30-16:30 (closed 25 Dec and 1 Jan); non-resident entry about SCR 450 for ages 12+, under-12s free, cards and EUR/USD accepted. Three loop trails, the shortest ~1 km and flat — fine for a 5-year-old. Go at 08:30 for cool air, birdsong and no tour groups; guided walks available at the gate · Kids: All ages — flat, shaded main path

places.name: L'Union Estate
places.near: 10 min by bike (or ox-cart/taxi) south from La Passe jetty on La Digue; one ticket booth for both the estate and the beach
places.notes: Ticket/access per lunionestate.com and 2026 Tripadvisor Union Estate Park reviews.
places.famousFor: The old copra and vanilla plantation that guards Anse Source d'Argent: ox-driven copra mill, vanilla walk, plantation house, boatyard and a giant-tortoise enclosure
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 4.2 ★ (1,142) · Ticket about SCR 150-300 pp (reports differ after a 2026 rise), valid all day with re-entry, cards accepted at the gate. Cover the estate first, then the beach in late-afternoon light. Bikes can be ridden in and left at the racks; the Union Rock granite monolith is right beside the copra mill · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — tortoise pen is a hit

places.name: Veuve Nature Reserve
places.area: La Digue — La Passe / Anse Reunion
places.near: 5-10 min bike ride inland from La Passe jetty on La Digue; signposted from the main road
places.notes: Hours/fees per SPGA and SeyVillas Veuve Reserve pages.
places.famousFor: The last stronghold of the Seychelles paradise flycatcher ('veuve') — a black bird with an absurdly long tail, found nowhere else in numbers
places.goodToKnow: ⭐ 3.8 ★ (18) · Open Mon-Fri 08:00-16:00, Sat 09:00-15:00, closed Sunday; about SCR 150 pp, or SCR 200 including a guided walk (guided tours Mon-Fri 10:30 and 14:30, over-12s). Early morning gives the best sightings. Flat, shaded and short — a good cool-down between beaches · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — flat 30-min shaded loop
places.address: Veuve Special Reserve, La Digue, Seychelles

places.name: St Pierre Islet Snorkel Stop
places.near: 10-15 min by boat from Anse Volbert / Cote d'Or, always as part of a Curieuse or island-hopping day trip; no landing on the islet itself
places.notes: Tour inclusion and conditions per Praslin Curieuse/St Pierre excursion operators.
places.famousFor: The postcard granite islet crowned with palms — the best easy snorkelling stop in the inner islands, thick with parrotfish, sergeant majors and the odd turtle
places.goodToKnow: Included in Curieuse day tours (about EUR 75-95); marine-park fee applies. You snorkel straight off the boat in open water, so weak swimmers need a vest — ask the operator for child-size masks and floats when booking. Visibility best Apr-May and Oct-Nov; can be choppy in the trade-wind months · Location needs verification · Kids: 7+ swimmers; younger stay aboard
places.address: St Pierre Islet, off Praslin, Seychelles

places.name: Anse Marron Guided Hike
places.near: Guided tours meet at Grand Anse or La Passe; roughly 2 hours each way on foot around the southern coast. Independent access is not permitted
places.notes: Guide requirement and difficulty per Sunny Trail Guide/SeyVillas and Anse Marron hiking guides.
places.famousFor: La Digue's secret beach — a natural rock-walled swimming pool reached only by squeezing between granite boulders and wading tidal pools with a licensed guide
places.goodToKnow: Guide is compulsory and genuinely necessary — trails are unmarked and sections disappear at high tide; Sunny Trail Guide is the best-known operator. Half-day, timed to the tide, water shoes essential, no shade and no facilities. Not suitable for the 5, 9 or 11 year-olds · Location needs verification · Kids: Teens only — boulder scramble

places.name: Seychelles National Botanical Gardens
places.near: Mont Fleuri Road, ~10 min walk south of Victoria centre or a short taxi/bus hop; easy add-on to a Victoria market morning
places.notes: Fee/hours per Tripadvisor 2026 reviews and Outlook Travel garden feature.
places.famousFor: A century-old 6-hectare garden in the capital with coco de mer palms, an orchid house, a fruit-bat colony and a walk-in Aldabra giant-tortoise pen
places.goodToKnow: Open daily about 08:00-17:00; entry around SCR 100 (about EUR 7.50) for non-residents, with a small extra charge (about EUR 5) to feed the tortoises. Allow 1-1.5 hours; shaded, stroller-friendly paths and a cafe. Best early when the tortoises are active and it is still cool · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — feed the tortoises
places.address: Mont Fleuri Road, Victoria, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Le Jardin du Roi Spice Garden
places.near: 2 km up a signposted hill road above Anse Royale on Mahe's south-east coast; ~20 min drive from the airport, taxi recommended as the lane is steep
places.notes: Fee, hours and menu prices per Jardin du Roi listings and Tripadvisor 2026.
places.famousFor: An 18th-century-style spice plantation in the hills — vanilla, nutmeg, cinnamon and pepper on self-guided trails, plus giant tortoises and a hilltop Creole restaurant with a huge coastal view
places.goodToKnow: Open daily about 10:00-17:00; entry around EUR 8 per visitor, children under 12 free (SCR rates for residents). Garden Walk, Medicinal Path and Rainforest Trail are all self-guided; guided hikes need 24h notice. The restaurant does spice-flavoured ice creams and a Sunday Planteur lunch (about SCR 289 adult / SCR 180 child) — a good cool-hour stop after a south-coast beach morning · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — under-12s often free

places.name: Takamaka Rum Distillery (La Plaine St Andre)
places.area: Mahe — Pointe au Sel, east coast
places.near: La Plaine St Andre, Pointe au Sel on Mahe's east coast; ~15 min drive south of the airport on the coast road
places.notes: Hours, tour times and tasting price per takamakarum.com and seychelles.com listing.
places.famousFor: A restored 1792 plantation house — heritage museum, medicinal garden, colonial ruins and two resident Aldabra tortoises named Taka and Maka, alongside the island's rum distillery
places.goodToKnow: Open Mon-Sat about 10:30-16:30; entry and the guided tour are free (tours Mon-Fri 11:00, 13:00, 15:00), rum tasting about SCR 150 pp. Alcohol is central to the tour, so a Muslim family may prefer to skip the tasting and just walk the heritage house, gardens and tortoises, or skip the site entirely; the food truck and grounds are open to all · Location needs verification · Kids: Grounds fine for all; tour is 15+
places.address: La Plaine St Andre, Pointe au Sel, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Sauzier Waterfall
places.near: Entrance is off the road beside the large church at Port Glaud lagoon, west Mahe; ~40 min drive from Victoria, often combined with Port Launay beach
places.notes: Fee and access per Tripadvisor Sauzier Waterfall reviews and Mahe waterfall guides.
places.famousFor: A jungle waterfall dropping into a deep dark pool five minutes from the road — the easiest freshwater swim on Mahe
places.goodToKnow: Small entry fee to non-residents, about SCR 50 adult / SCR 25 under-12 (collected on the path). Flow is strongest Dec-Mar; can be a trickle late in the dry season. Rocks are very slippery — proper shoes, and hold the little ones' hands. Local 'guides' may offer help for a tip; agree or decline up front · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — slippery rock, 5-min

places.name: Port Launay Marine National Park
places.area: Mahe — Port Launay / Baie Ternay, west
places.near: West Mahe past Port Glaud, next to Constance Ephelia; ~40 min drive from the airport. Baie Ternay itself is reached by boat or a walk from Port Launay
places.notes: Marine park and family suitability per Mahe west-coast beach and snorkelling guides.
places.famousFor: A protected west-coast bay with the calmest snorkelling water on Mahe and, Aug-Oct, a chance of whale sharks passing offshore
places.goodToKnow: Beach access is free; snorkel boats into Baie Ternay charge a marine-park fee. Shallow, sheltered and shaded by takamaka trees — the gentlest snorkel spot on Mahe for a 5- and 9-year-old. Bring your own masks; rental is limited. Pair it with Sauzier Waterfall for a full west-coast day · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — calm, shallow, protected

places.name: Blue Sea Divers / Big Blue Divers (Discover Scuba)
places.near: Both are on the Beau Vallon beach road, ~25 min from the airport; free hotel pickup within the Beau Vallon area
places.notes: Schedules, courses and pickup per blueseadivers.com and Big Blue Divers listings.
places.famousFor: Beau Vallon's two long-running dive schools — first-time 'Discover Scuba' sessions in a sheltered bay, plus snorkelling excursions to Baie Ternay and the Ennerdale wreck for the rest of the family
places.goodToKnow: Boats leave 09:00 for a two-tank morning (back ~12:30) and 14:00 for a single afternoon dive. Discover Scuba is a ~3-hour beginner programme with a qualified instructor and small groups — minimum age is normally 10 (PADI Bubblemaker from 8 at some centres, ask). Book a day ahead; best visibility Apr-May and Oct-Nov · Location needs verification · Kids: Scuba 10+; snorkel all ages

places.name: Sunset Catamaran Cruise from Eden Island
places.near: Departs Eden Island Marina, ~10 min from the airport and 15 min from Victoria; charters also start from Beau Vallon by beach tender
places.notes: Charter format and indicative pricing per Eden Island charter operators (Getmyboat, Exotic Boat Charter).
places.famousFor: A private late-afternoon sail along Mahe's north coast past the Sainte Anne islands, with the sun dropping behind the granite peaks
places.goodToKnow: Private sunset charters typically run about 14:30-18:00 depending on sunset; day charters for up to 6 start around USD 1,400 with skipper, food, soft drinks and snorkel gear, extra guests roughly USD 50 each — so a family of 7 fits one boat. Under-6s often free. Book a private boat rather than a shared one; most operators are alcohol-optional on request · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — under-6s often free

places.name: Deep-Sea Fishing Charter (Eden Island / Beau Vallon)
places.near: Charter boats berth at Eden Island Marina and work off Beau Vallon; hotel pickup usually included
places.notes: Charter base and season information per Eden Island Marina and Seychelles charter operators.
places.famousFor: Seychelles' drop-off and bank fishing — sailfish, dorado, wahoo, tuna and giant trevally, with many skippers happy to have the catch cooked back at your hotel
places.goodToKnow: Half-day (about 4h) is the sensible first outing with kids; full-day trolling runs 8 hours offshore. Best big-game season is roughly Oct-Apr; seas are roughest Jun-Aug. Prices are per boat, not per person — confirm rods, bait, ice, drinks and whether tag-and-release applies. Bring motion-sickness tablets for the 9- and 11-year-olds · Location needs verification · Kids: 11+ (swell); half-day for beginners

places.name: Hawksbill Turtle Nesting Watch (Oct-Mar)
places.near: Guided beach patrols on Cousin Island (boat from Praslin, weekdays only) and Curieuse; several Mahe and outer-island resorts run their own patrols along the south coast
places.notes: Season and etiquette per Nature Seychelles and BirdLife Cousin Island turtle reports.
places.famousFor: One of the few places on earth where hawksbill turtles nest in daylight — females hauling up the beach, and hatchlings running for the sea between December and March
places.goodToKnow: Season runs roughly October to March (occasional nests from August and into early April); hatchlings mostly December-March. Only ever watch with conservation staff — no flash, no torches, stay behind the turtle and never touch tracks or nests. Cousin's warden-led walks are the most reliable structured option · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — quiet, patient watching

places.name: The Sanctuary at Roche Caiman
places.near: Roche Caiman, between the housing estate and the National Sports Complex, ~5 min drive south of Victoria and next to Eden Island
places.notes: Site description and management per natureseychelles.org Sanctuary page.
places.famousFor: Seychelles' only urban wetland reserve — a reclaimed lagoon by the national stadium now full of herons, waders, terrapins and dragonflies, with a heritage garden
places.goodToKnow: Small, quiet and managed by Nature Seychelles; opening hours are limited and it can close for works, so check before going. Bring binoculars and mosquito repellent. Best early morning. A useful 45-minute stop if you have a slow morning near Eden Island rather than a destination in itself · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — flat, 45 min, free-ish

places.name: Seychelles Natural History Museum
places.near: Independence Avenue in central Victoria, 2 min walk from the Clock Tower and the market
places.notes: Hours per seychellesnationalmuseums.org and Victoria museum listings.
places.famousFor: Old-school island natural history — coco de mer nuts, the giant tortoise and skeleton displays, endemic birds and geology explaining why these granite islands exist at all
places.goodToKnow: Open roughly Mon-Thu 08:30-16:30, Fri and Sat 08:30-12:00, closed Sunday; small entry fee. Dated but genuinely useful before Vallee de Mai — the kids will understand the coco de mer story much better afterwards. Combine with the market and Clock Tower in one Victoria morning · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — small, 45 min max

places.name: Seychelles National Museum of History
places.near: Francis Rachel Street in central Victoria, opposite the Clock Tower; walking distance from the market and Kenwyn House
places.notes: Hours per seychellesnationalmuseums.org opening-hours page.
places.famousFor: The story of the islands from first landing and the Stone of Possession to slavery, exile and independence, in the restored former Supreme Court building
places.goodToKnow: Open Mon 09:30-12:30, Tue-Fri 09:30-16:30 (closed 12:00-13:00), Sat 09:30-12:30, closed Sunday and public holidays; modest entry fee. Air-conditioned and well laid out — a good hour when the midday sun is too much for the beach · Location needs verification · Kids: 11+ — text-heavy but well done
places.address: Francis Rachel Street, Victoria, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Victoria Clock Tower (Lorloz)
places.near: Junction of Independence Avenue and Francis Rachel Street, central Victoria; all Mahe bus routes converge two streets away
places.notes: Landmark description per Victoria city guides and national museum walking routes.
places.famousFor: The 1903 silver clock tower modelled on London's Little Ben — the symbolic centre of the world's smallest capital city
places.goodToKnow: Free, always open, on a busy roundabout — hold small children's hands and shoot from the pavement corner. Everything in Victoria (market, museums, Kenwyn House, cathedral) is within a 10-minute walk, so start the city morning here around 08:30 · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — 10-min photo stop

places.name: Cat Cocos Inter-Island Ferry
places.near: Departs the Inter Island Quay in Victoria, Mahe (~20 min from the airport); Mahe-Praslin ~75 min, Mahe-La Digue ~1h45 with a 15-min Praslin stop. The smaller Cat Rose covers Praslin-La Digue in ~15 min
places.notes: Fares and timings per seyferry.com Cat Cocos schedule and pricing pages (2025-2026).
places.famousFor: The fast catamaran that links the three main islands — the practical backbone of any Mahe + Praslin + La Digue trip, and a scenic ride past the granite islets
places.goodToKnow: 2026 indicative one-way fares Mahe-Praslin: economy main cabin about EUR 56 adult / EUR 27 child (2-12), upper deck EUR 62/33, business EUR 77/44; Mahe-La Digue economy about EUR 68/39. Book online well ahead for a group of 7, especially Dec-Jan and Jul-Aug. Crossings are bumpiest in the south-east trades (Jun-Aug) — bring tablets for the younger kids · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — sit upper deck if queasy
places.address: Inter Island Quay, Victoria, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Sir Selwyn Selwyn-Clarke Market
places.near: Market Street, central Victoria, 3 min walk from the Clock Tower; all island bus routes end at the Victoria terminus nearby
places.notes: Hours, Saturday advice and renovation move per Culture Trip and Inside Seychelles market guides.
places.famousFor: Victoria's 1840 covered market — reef fish on ice, tropical fruit, vanilla pods, cinnamon bark, Creole spice mixes and souvenir stalls on the upper level
places.goodToKnow: Best on Saturday morning from about 06:00 (winds down by early afternoon); weekday mornings are calmer. Note the market has been under renovation with trading temporarily relocated to the former STC Supermarket building in Victoria — check where it is trading before you go. Cash SCR is easiest; bargaining is mild. Buy vanilla and cinnamon here rather than at the airport · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — busy, hold hands

places.name: Eden Plaza
places.near: Eden Island, linked to Mahe by a short bridge; ~10 min from the airport and 4 km from Victoria, taxi or bus
places.notes: Facilities and public-access detail per Eden Island Marina and EILA official pages.
places.famousFor: The largest shopping centre in Seychelles — 50-plus shops, supermarket, pharmacy, banks, spa and a marina promenade of waterfront restaurants
places.goodToKnow: The plaza, marina village promenade and public walkways are open to everyone (the residential canals are not). The supermarket here is the best-stocked in the country — worth a stop for villa self-catering, snacks and baby supplies. Also the departure point for most Sainte Anne boat trips, so easy to combine · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — air-con rainy-day plan
places.address: Eden Plaza, Eden Island, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Kenwyn House
places.near: Francis Rachel Street, central Victoria, a 2-minute walk from the Clock Tower
places.notes: Hours and offering per Gran Kaz Kenwyn House page and Seychelles News Agency gallery report.
places.famousFor: An 1855 French-colonial national monument turned duty-free jeweller and gallery — South African diamonds and precious stones downstairs, Seychellois artists upstairs, tropical garden cafe outside
places.goodToKnow: Open Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat 09:00-13:00. Free to walk in and look at the house and gallery — no obligation to buy. Prices are duty-free, so genuinely competitive for coloured stones; ask for the certificate. The garden is a cool, quiet break in the middle of a Victoria walking morning · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — short, calm, 30 min
places.address: Francis Rachel Street, Victoria, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Domaine de Val des Pres (Craft Village)
places.near: Au Cap on Mahe's east coast, ~10 min drive south of the airport on the coast road; on the main bus route
places.notes: Hours, layout and free entry per Seychelles Heritage Foundation and seychelles.travel listings.
places.famousFor: A heritage plantation turned craft village: the 1870s Gran Kaz plantation house, a period Creole cottage, twelve artisan workshops and the Maison de Coco selling everything made from coconut
places.goodToKnow: Open daily about 09:30-17:00, free entry to the village (the plantation house may charge). The most reliable place on Mahe for genuine local craft — model boats, pottery, batik, coconut-oil products and spices — rather than imported souvenirs. Pomme Cannelle restaurant on site for a Creole lunch · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — free, shaded, easy

places.name: Michael Adams Studio
places.area: Mahe — Anse aux Poules Bleues, Baie Lazare
places.near: Anse aux Poules Bleues, Baie Lazare, south-west Mahe; ~30 min drive from the airport, signposted off the coast road
places.notes: Hours and contact per michaeladamsart.com visit page and Petit Fute listing.
places.famousFor: Seychelles' best-known artist (MBE, painting here since 1972) — riotous green silkscreens of the jungle, sold from the studio at his own home, alongside work by his children Tristan and Alyssa
places.goodToKnow: Usually open weekdays 10:30-13:00 and 13:30-16:00, Saturday 10:30-12:00, closed Sunday and public holidays. Email adams@seychelles.net or call +248 4361006 first — it is a private home and hours can shift. Silkscreens and small prints travel well rolled; the single best premium souvenir from Seychelles · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — quiet, 30 min, look-only
places.address: Anse aux Poules Bleues, Baie Lazare, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: George Camille Art Gallery
places.near: Anse Gaulette on La Digue's west coast road; 10-15 min by bike south from La Passe jetty, past L'Union Estate
places.notes: Gallery location and background per Lonely Planet and georgecamille.com biography.
places.famousFor: The island gallery of George Camille, Seychelles' other great painter — etchings, watercolours and collages of Creole houses, fishermen and frangipani, opened here in 2004
places.goodToKnow: Small ground-floor gallery under a three-storey Creole guesthouse; prints from modest prices up to serious originals, and staff will pack work for flying. Camille's Sunstroke Studio outlets on Mahe and La Digue carry the cheaper prints and cards. Hours are informal — go mid-morning on a weekday · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — 20-min stop by bike

places.name: Zaans Museum
places.near: Zaandam, beside Zaandijk Zaanse Schans station; train from Amsterdam then short walk
places.order: The patchwork green-and-white gabled facade; nearby windmills and wooden houses along the Zaan
places.notes: Saved POI
places.famousFor: Museum beside the Zaanse Schans whose facade stacks dozens of traditional green Zaan house gables
places.goodToKnow: Museum paid; Zaanse Schans windmills free outdoors; early visit beats day-trip crowds · Location needs verification

places.name: Nid d'Aigle Viewpoint
places.area: La Digue — Belle Vue, island summit
places.near: From La Passe ride a bike about 20 min up the very steep inland road (most people push the last stretch) then walk ~15 min on the forest track; local pickups will drive you up for a fee
places.notes: Access and altitude per 2026 La Digue island guides.
places.famousFor: La Digue's 333 m summit — the whole island, its Creole rooftops and jetty below, with Praslin, Felicite and the sister islands on the horizon
places.goodToKnow: Free, open access. Go for late-afternoon light or early morning; the road is brutal in midday heat, so take the drive-up option with younger kids. The little Belle Vue snack kiosk near the top is a reliable stop for a cold drink · Location needs verification · Kids: 11+ — steep 15-min final climb
places.address: Nid d'Aigle, Belle Vue, La Digue, Seychelles

places.name: Anse Source d'Argent Boulder Field (Anse Pierrot)
places.area: La Digue — south end of L'Union beach
places.near: Enter through L'Union Estate on La Digue, then keep walking 10-20 min south past the first bays towards Anse Pierrot; passable at low tide, wet at high
places.notes: Shooting notes from La Digue photography guides; coordinates from Wikipedia.
places.famousFor: The world's most photographed granite: house-sized weathered boulders standing in ankle-deep turquoise water, glowing pink at golden hour
places.goodToKnow: The classic frames are all at the far southern end — the first 200 m are the crowded ones. Best light is 16:00 to sunset with the sun behind the boulders; low tide exposes the sand bars and reflections. Estate gate closes late afternoon, so check the last-entry time before planning a sunset shoot · Kids: All ages — barefoot boulder hopping
places.address: Anse Pierrot, L'Union Estate, La Digue, Seychelles

places.name: Anse Lazio Viewpoint (Chevalier Bay Headland)
places.area: Praslin — above Anse Lazio car park
places.near: Walk up the short path over the headland from the Anse Lazio car park on north-west Praslin; the restaurant terrace at the north end gives a second, easier angle
places.notes: Viewpoint and light advice from Praslin beach and photography guides; coordinates from Wikipedia.
places.famousFor: The elevated frame over Anse Lazio's whole crescent — takamaka canopy in the foreground, granite headlands, and every shade of blue in the bay
places.goodToKnow: Free. Morning light (before 10:00) is best for the water colour and the beach is empty; by noon the tour boats arrive. The rocks at both ends give clean foreground framing. Watch footing on wet granite after rain · Kids: All ages — 5-min path from car park

places.name: Copolia Summit Granite Dome
places.area: Mahe — Sans Souci, Morne Seychellois NP
places.near: Trailhead opposite Copolia Lodge on Sans Souci Road; ~15 min taxi from Victoria then a 45-90 min climb
places.notes: Access, fee and conditions per SPGA/Seychelles News Agency trail information.
places.famousFor: A bare granite slab 497 m above the capital giving the definitive Mahe photograph — Victoria, Eden Island and the whole Sainte Anne archipelago laid out below
places.goodToKnow: Trail open 08:00-16:00, about SCR 100 pp for non-residents over 12, card only. Go at opening — cloud builds over the summit by late morning and the granite gets blindingly hot. Pitcher plants near the top are the macro shot. No railings on the slab: keep children well back from the edge · Location needs verification · Kids: Best 9+ (steep 1.5h round trip)

places.name: Mission Lodge (Venn's Town) Viewpoint
places.near: On the Sans Souci cross-island road between Victoria and Port Glaud; ~20 min drive from Victoria, parking at the gate then a 5-min level walk through the avenue of trees
places.notes: Fee and UNESCO status per Seychelles Nation article and Seychelles Heritage Foundation.
places.famousFor: A ruined 1876 school for liberated slave children on a mountain ridge, with a covered belvedere framing the west coast, Morne Seychellois and the mimosa-filled valleys
places.goodToKnow: About SCR 100 entry for non-Seychellois, free for under-12s (Seychelles Heritage Foundation); UNESCO tentative-list site since 2013. Late afternoon light over the west coast is the best, and it is the easiest big view on Mahe — no hiking involved, so it works for the 5-year-old and for anyone skipping Copolia · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — drive up, flat, 30 min
places.address: Sans Souci Road, Venn's Town, Mahe, Seychelles

places.name: Anse Major Trail Coastal Overlook
places.near: Walk the Anse Major trail from the road end at Danzil, Bel Ombre; the open glacis section starts ~20 min in
places.notes: Trail character and boat return per Anse Major hiking guides and Savoy Resort blog.
places.famousFor: The bare glacis granite section midway along the trail, looking down over cobalt water, Therese Island and a coastline with no road and no buildings
places.goodToKnow: Free. Shoot in the first two hours after sunrise or the last two before sunset — midday is brutally exposed with no shade. Return by the hourly taxi-boat (about SCR 150 pp) to save the family a second hot hour on foot. Sea spray and salt: keep the lens covered on windy days · Location needs verification · Kids: 5+ with breaks — exposed, no shade

places.name: L'Union Estate Copra Mill & Union Rock
places.near: Inside L'Union Estate on La Digue, on the path between the entrance and Anse Source d'Argent; bike in from La Passe (10 min)
places.notes: Site contents and ticket per lunionestate.com and La Digue visitor guides.
places.famousFor: The ox-turned copra mill under palms and the enormous smooth granite monolith of Union Rock — the best 'old Seychelles' frames on La Digue
places.goodToKnow: Covered by the same estate ticket (about SCR 150-300, all-day re-entry). Morning light filters through the palms over the mill; the vanilla plantation and colonial plantation house are a two-minute walk on. Do this on the way in, then hit the beach for late-afternoon light on one ticket · Location needs verification · Kids: All ages — flat, shaded, 30 min

places.name: Sheikh Mohamed bin Khalifa Al-Nahyan Mosque (Victoria)
places.area: Mahé — Victoria, Bel Air (La Poudrière Road)
places.near: La Poudrière Road, Bel Air, on the southern edge of central Victoria — a 5–10 minute walk uphill from the clock tower; any Victoria-bound bus or taxi drops you in town.
places.notes: Wikipedia 'Sheikh Mohamed bin Khalifa Mosque' + Seychelles News Agency article on the Muslim community; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The country's first and main mosque, built September 1982 and renovated in 2013 — gold dome, capacity ~600, and the place where Jumu'ah is held for the whole of Mahé.
places.goodToKnow: Busiest by far at Friday noon prayer; khutbah is delivered in Arabic with the talk in Creole/English. Muslims are ~1–1.6% of the population, so this is the community hub — plan Friday around Victoria. A second, smaller mosque was completed in 2013 in the Mont Fleuri district on the edge of town.
places.address: La Poudrière Road, Bel Air, Victoria, Mahé

places.name: Praslin Mosque
places.area: Praslin — Grand Anse (Grand'Anse–Baie Sainte Anne Road)
places.near: On the main Grand'Anse–Baie Sainte Anne road at Grand Anse, Praslin's main village; ~10 min by car from Baie Ste Anne jetty and on the SPTC bus route.
places.notes: OpenStreetMap 'Praslin Mosque' node + Salatomatic/Tripadvisor Praslin mosque threads; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The only mosque on Praslin — small but adequate, open for the daily prayers and for Jumu'ah; the only prayer facility outside Mahé.
places.goodToKnow: Be accurate in your planning: there is NO mosque on La Digue. If you are on La Digue for Friday, either pray at the accommodation or take the ~15-min Cat Rose ferry across to Praslin in the morning. Prayer times shift only slightly year-round this close to the equator (Seychelles is UTC+4, same as UAE).
places.address: Grand'Anse Praslin – Baie Sainte Anne Road, Grand Anse, Praslin

places.name: STC Hypermarket (Bois de Rose)
places.area: Mahé — Bois de Rose / Mont Fleuri, Victoria
places.near: Bois de Rose complex on Bois de Rose Avenue / Coast Guard Road, ~5 min south of central Victoria by car; all south-bound buses pass it.
places.notes: STC official retail page stcl.sc + evendo/petitfute listings for hours; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The largest retail space in Seychelles and the state trading company's flagship — the one place to do a genuine weekly shop for a family of 7 at near-local prices.
places.goodToKnow: Roughly Mon–Sat 08:00/09:00–19:00/20:00 and Sunday morning only (sources differ — confirm on the day). Bring bags. Almost everything is imported so prices are high; buy local fruit, fish and eggs at the market instead. ISPC on the same Bois de Rose Avenue (approx. -4.63274, 55.46480) is the better source for fresh produce, deli, cheese and imported goods.
places.address: Bois de Rose Complex, Bois de Rose Avenue, Mont Fleuri, Mahé

places.name: Spar Supermarket, Eden Plaza (Eden Island)
places.area: Mahé — Eden Island (Marina Drive, Eden Plaza)
places.near: Eden Island causeway off the East Coast Road at Roche Caiman, ~10 min from Victoria and ~10 min from the airport; taxis and buses both serve it.
places.notes: Eden Plaza official site edenplaza.sc + OpenStreetMap Spar nodes on Marina Drive and Francis Rachel Street.
places.famousFor: The best-stocked supermarket for visitors — inside the Eden Plaza mall on the marina, with a pharmacy, cafés, ATMs, phone shops and restaurants all in the same air-conditioned building.
places.goodToKnow: Open later and on Sundays when central Victoria is shut — the single most useful one-stop for a self-catering family. There is a second Spar in town on Francis Rachel Street (approx. -4.62443, 55.45255). Eden Pharmacy is in the same plaza.
places.address: Eden Plaza, Marina Drive, Eden Island, Mahé

places.name: Praslin & La Digue groceries (Ramajayam / Mas / STC La Digue)
places.area: Praslin — Grand Anse & Baie Ste Anne; La Digue — La Passe
places.near: Praslin: Ramajayam at Grand Anse (approx. -4.32664, 55.71507) and Mas at Anse Kerlan (approx. -4.31285, 55.68684), both on the Grand'Anse–Baie Sainte Anne road; A-One and Darling are smaller convenience shops nearer Baie Ste Anne. La Digue: STC in the Gregoire's building on Allée Kersley, on the road behind La Digue Island Lodge — walk or cycle from the jetty.
places.notes: seychelles.cc La Digue shopping guide + OpenStreetMap supermarket nodes for Praslin and La Digue; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The main food shops on the two smaller islands: Ramajayam and Mas supermarkets on Praslin, and the STC in the Gregoire's building — the biggest shop on La Digue.
places.goodToKnow: Stock and hours are much thinner than Mahé and prices higher — buy bulk staples, nappies, sun cream and any special dietary items on Mahé before you ferry across. There is an ATM outside the STC on La Digue and an MCB ATM near the jetty; Milena's shop in La Passe covers odds and ends.
places.address: STC, Allée Kersley, La Réunion / La Passe, La Digue

places.name: Halal food sourcing in Seychelles (SeyHa – Seychelles Halal Association)
places.area: Seychelles — all islands (association based in Victoria, Mahé)
places.near: No retail outlet — contact through the mosques in Victoria; ask at the Sheikh Mohamed bin Khalifa Mosque for current halal-supplier information.
places.notes: SeyHa (seyha.org) association description + HalalTrip / MuslimTravelGirl Seychelles guides on the absence of certification.
places.famousFor: The non-profit set up in 2018 by the mosques and Islamic societies of Seychelles to help consumers find halal products and services — the only halal reference body in the country.
places.goodToKnow: Be realistic: there is NO dedicated halal butcher and no formal halal certification for restaurants in Seychelles. What works in practice — buy packaged frozen chicken and beef at STC/Spar/ISPC and read the label (much of it is imported from Dubai/Brazil and carries a halal mark), and lean on seafood, which is everywhere and excellent. Assume no restaurant is certified; pork and alcohol are common on Creole menus, so ask before ordering. · Location needs verification

places.name: Behram's Pharmacy (Orion Mall, Victoria)
places.area: Mahé — Victoria (Palm Street, Orion Mall building)
places.near: Ground floor, Orion Mall building, Palm Street, central Victoria — a 3-minute walk from the clock tower.
places.notes: Petit Futé + Commercial Register of Seychelles listings for Behram's Pharmacy (address, hours, phone); coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: Seychelles' longest-running private pharmacy chain (since 1977, Seychellois pharmacists UK-trained) — the default pharmacy in central Victoria.
places.goodToKnow: Mon–Fri 08:30–16:45, Sat 08:15–12:30, closed Sunday — Victoria pharmacies keep short hours, so restock before the weekend. There is a second Behram's at Beau Vallon on the North Coast Road (approx. -4.61701, 55.42970) and one at Plaisance/Les Mamelles. Bring your own supply of anything prescription-only; stock is limited.
places.address: Ground Floor, Orion Mall Building, Palm Street, Victoria, Mahé

places.name: Eden Pharmacy (Eden Plaza)
places.area: Mahé — Eden Island (Marina Drive, Eden Plaza)
places.near: Unit 1, Marina Drive, Eden Plaza, Eden Island — off the East Coast Road at Roche Caiman, ~10 min from Victoria or the airport.
places.notes: OpenStreetMap 'Eden Pharmacy' node, Marina Drive, Eden Island + Eden Plaza shop directory; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The pharmacy inside the Eden Plaza mall — the most convenient one for visitors, with longer and weekend hours than the Victoria town pharmacies.
places.goodToKnow: Same building as the Spar, cafés and ATMs, so it's the single best 'we forgot something' stop with kids in the car. Stock sun cream, rehydration salts, mosquito repellent and any paediatric medicines here before island-hopping — Praslin and La Digue each have only one pharmacy.
places.address: 1 Marina Drive, Eden Plaza, Eden Island, Mahé

places.name: D'Offay Pharmacy (Beau Vallon, Praslin & La Digue)
places.area: Mahé — Beau Vallon & Bois de Rose; Praslin — Baie Ste Anne; La Digue — La Passe
places.near: Beau Vallon: Palmont Building on the North Coast Road strip. Victoria: Bois de Rose Avenue. Praslin: Baie Ste Anne. La Digue: La Passe, near the jetty.
places.notes: KOEK.sc + Commercial Register listings for D'Offay Pharmacy and seyvillas health guide / Seychelles Nation 'Pharmacies around still open'; no verified coordinates, left blank.
places.famousFor: The only pharmacy chain with outlets on all three main islands — and effectively the sole pharmacy on both Praslin and La Digue.
places.goodToKnow: Beau Vallon branch runs long hours (about 08:30–19:30 daily); the Praslin and La Digue outlets are 09:00–18:00 Mon–Sat and closed Sunday. Outside those hours the only option on Praslin/La Digue is the island hospital. Two more pharmacies exist at Grand Anse, Praslin (Absolue and Compagnie Pharmaceutique). · Location needs verification
places.address: Palmont Building, Beau Vallon, Mahé (plus Bois de Rose, Baie Ste Anne & La Passe branches)

places.name: Seychelles Hospital (Victoria Hospital), Mont Fleuri
places.near: Hospital Road, Mont Fleuri, ~5 min south of central Victoria; signposted off Bois de Rose Avenue. Taxis know it as 'Victoria Hospital'.
places.notes: seyvillas.com Seychelles health guide (facility names and phone numbers); coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The national referral hospital and the only full A&E in the country — every serious case on any island ends up here.
places.goodToKnow: Other public facilities: Anse Royale Hospital in the south of Mahé (+248 437 1222, approx. -4.73997, 55.51687), Baie Sainte Anne Hospital on Praslin (+248 423 2333, approx. -4.33842, 55.75642) and Logan Hospital on La Digue (+248 423 4255). Private clinics exist in Victoria/Eden but are limited. Travel insurance with medical repatriation cover is essential — complex cases are flown out.
places.address: Hospital Road, Mont Fleuri, Victoria, Mahé

places.name: Emergency services 999 / 151 and the diving recompression chamber
places.near: Both numbers work from any Seychelles SIM; save them plus your hotel's number before you land. Dive emergencies are coordinated through your dive centre and A&E.
places.notes: seyvillas.com health guide (999/151) + DAN Southern Africa chamber-network material on Mahé and Silhouette; no single coordinate applies, left blank.
places.famousFor: 999 is the general emergency number (police/fire/ambulance); 151 reaches Accident & Emergency directly at the hospital in Victoria.
places.goodToKnow: Recompression (hyperbaric) chamber facilities in Seychelles are on Mahé — the hospital in Victoria is the nearest chamber for anyone diving off Mahé, Praslin or La Digue; a further DAN-listed chamber is attached to the resort medical centre on Silhouette Island. There is NO chamber on Praslin or La Digue, so a dive accident there means an evacuation to Mahé — factor that into any diving with the family and check your insurance covers hyperbaric treatment. · Location needs verification
places.address: Nationwide (A&E at Seychelles Hospital, Mont Fleuri, Victoria, Mahé)

places.name: SIM & mobile data on arrival — Cable & Wireless / Airtel (SEZ Airport)
places.area: Mahé — Seychelles International Airport, Pointe Larue
places.near: Arrivals hall, Seychelles International Airport, Pointe Larue, ~10 min from Victoria. Town branches: Airtel on Huteau Lane, Victoria (approx. -4.62113, 55.45240); Cable & Wireless at Beau Vallon on the North Coast Road (approx. -4.61696, 55.42970).
places.notes: roafly / 4stogo / gigago Seychelles SIM guides (airport kiosks, tourist plans, eSIM limits); airport coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: Operator kiosks in/near the arrivals area at SEZ — the fastest way to be connected before you leave the terminal; the two networks are Cable & Wireless (CWS) and Airtel Seychelles.
places.goodToKnow: Typical tourist packs: Airtel ~EUR 20 for 5GB + local minutes for 30 days; Cable & Wireless ~EUR 25 for 10GB with unlimited local calls/texts. Bring your passport — registration is required. Local operators do not yet sell eSIMs to prepaid customers, so either take a physical SIM at the airport or install a third-party travel eSIM (Airalo etc.) before departure. Coverage is good on Mahé/Praslin/La Digue and patchy in the mountains and on boats.
places.address: Arrivals, Seychelles International Airport (SEZ), Pointe Larue, Mahé

places.name: Car hire at Seychelles International Airport (SEZ)
places.area: Mahé — Seychelles International Airport, Pointe Larue
places.near: Desks are immediately outside the arrivals/customs gate; cars are in the terminal car park. Sixt runs roughly 06:00–midnight, Avis roughly 07:30–21:30 (shorter Sundays).
places.notes: seychellesinternationalairport.com car-rental page + Sixt/Avis Mahé branch pages for hours; airport coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: Avis, Hertz, Sixt, Thrifty and several local operators have desks right beside the customs exit in the terminal — a hire car is essentially compulsory for exploring Mahé with a big family.
places.goodToKnow: Drive on the LEFT. No motorways — rural limits are mostly 40 km/h, roads are narrow, steep and twisty with blind hillside bends; a small SUV is easier than a big van, and 7 people will need two cars or a minibus with driver. Book well ahead in high season. Cars are NOT worth hiring on Praslin for a short stay (taxis/buses cover it) and are pointless on La Digue, which is bicycles and electric buggies only.
places.address: Arrivals terminal, Seychelles International Airport, Anse des Genets, Pointe Larue, Mahé

places.name: Cat Cocos Ferry Terminal (Inter Island Quay, Victoria)
places.area: Mahé — Inter Island Quay, Victoria (Grandcourt Road / Laurrier Avenue)
places.near: Inter Island Quay on the Victoria waterfront, off Grandcourt Road; the Cat Cocos office is on Laurrier Avenue nearby. ~15 min by taxi from the airport. Praslin end is Baie Ste Anne Jetty (approx. -4.34686, 55.76575).
places.notes: seyferry.com / seychelles-ferry.com Cat Cocos schedule and fare pages; coordinates from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim.
places.famousFor: The fast catamaran link Mahé↔Praslin (~1 hr) and Mahé↔La Digue (with a short Praslin stop) — the standard way to island-hop without flying.
places.goodToKnow: Book online in advance — sailings sell out in high season and online booking closes about 28 hours before departure. Three classes (Economy Main, Economy Upper, Business); indicative 2026 one-way adult fares ~EUR 56 Mahé–Praslin and ~EUR 68 Mahé–La Digue, with child rates. Check in ~45–60 min early with luggage. The crossing can be rough — bring motion-sickness tablets for the children and pick the upper/business deck if anyone is prone to it.
places.address: Inter Island Quay, Grandcourt Road, Victoria, Mahé

places.name: Inter Island Ferry / Cat Rose (Praslin ↔ La Digue), La Passe
places.area: La Digue — La Passe jetty (Allée Kersley ticket office)
places.near: La Digue end: La Passe harbour in the middle of the village, with the Cat Rose ticket office on Allée Kersley. Praslin end: Baie Ste Anne Jetty. Cat Cocos boats from Mahé also call directly at La Passe.
places.notes: OpenStreetMap 'Cat Rose ferry ticket office' node, Allée Kersley, La Digue + seychelles-ferry.com booking pages.
places.famousFor: The short (~15 min) shuttle between Baie Ste Anne on Praslin and La Passe on La Digue — the only scheduled way onto La Digue, running many times a day.
places.goodToKnow: Book online ahead in high season and keep the Praslin↔La Digue connection at least 60–90 min clear of any Cat Cocos or flight connection — the small boat is the one most affected by swell and it is the leg most likely to be uncomfortable. On arrival at La Digue you walk out into the village; hire bicycles right at the jetty, and porters/ox-cart-style luggage transfers are available to guesthouses.
places.address: Cat Rose ferry ticket office, Allée Kersley, La Passe, La Digue

places.name: SPTC public buses & taxis
places.near: Main Mahé bus terminal is in central Victoria by the market; the airport taxi rank is directly outside both the domestic and international arrivals halls.
places.notes: SPTC official site sptc.sc (routes, fares, timetable) + welcomepickups/seychellesinternationalairport taxi fare pages; no single coordinate applies, left blank.
places.famousFor: SPTC is the sole public bus operator — 106 routes and 1,600+ daily journeys across Mahé and Praslin, at a flat SCR 5 per trip (SCR 8 air-conditioned); taxis are metered and available 24/7 at the airport rank.
places.goodToKnow: Buses are cheap and scenic but slow, crowded and awkward with 7 people, luggage or after dark — good for one-off hops, not a family's main transport. Taxis: the airport→Victoria run is roughly EUR 20; many drivers quote a flat fare instead of running the meter in high season, so agree the price before you set off and insist on the meter being reset. Taxis expect cash in SCR; paying in EUR/USD attracts a poor rate. No Uber/Careem — arrange returns through your hotel or keep a driver's number. · Location needs verification
places.address: Victoria bus terminal, Palm Street area, Victoria, Mahé

places.name: Currency, ATMs & card acceptance
places.area: Seychelles — Victoria, Eden Island, Beau Vallon, Praslin & La Digue
places.near: Bank branches and ATMs line Independence Avenue and Francis Rachel Street in Victoria; Eden Plaza has ATMs indoors; La Digue has an ATM outside the STC and an MCB machine near the jetty.
places.notes: seyvillas.com currency guide, koek.sc money-tips and Exiap Seychelles currency guide; no single coordinate applies, left blank.
places.famousFor: The Seychelles Rupee (SCR) is the currency; ATMs are clustered in Victoria, Eden Plaza, Beau Vallon, Baie Ste Anne on Praslin and by the jetty on La Digue.
places.goodToKnow: The reality: a two-track system. Resorts, dive centres, tour operators and car hire quote and take EUR/USD and cards; small guesthouses, takeaways, market stalls, buses and taxis want SCR cash. Most ATMs take Visa/Mastercard but add 2–5% in fees, and machines on Praslin/La Digue do run out — draw cash on Mahé. Keep small notes for taxis and market fruit. You may bring in up to SCR 2,000 and the equivalent of USD 10,000 in foreign currency without declaring; above that must be declared at customs. · Location needs verification
places.address: Victoria town centre & Eden Plaza, Mahé

places.name: Laundry — Mauricelavigne (Beau Vallon) & Orion Mall (Victoria)
places.near: Orion Mall on Constitution Avenue, central Victoria (approx. -4.61945, 55.45467); Mauricelavigne is on the Beau Vallon strip.
places.notes: Tripadvisor Mahé laundry threads + Mauricelavigne Laundry Facebook page and Seychelles YP laundry-services directory; no verified coordinates, left blank.
places.famousFor: The practical laundry options outside hotels: a laundry service at Orion Mall in central Victoria and Mauricelavigne Laundry at Beau Vallon (washing and drying, including sheets and towels).
places.goodToKnow: There are essentially no self-service laundromats — services charge per garment, which gets expensive fast for 7 people. Cheapest route is a self-catering villa or guesthouse with a washing machine (confirm before booking); hotel laundry is priced in EUR and is the most expensive option of all. Clothes dry very fast outdoors, but the humidity means damp swimwear needs air, not a bag. · Location needs verification
places.address: Orion Mall, Constitution Avenue, Victoria, Mahé; Mauricelavigne Laundry, Beau Vallon, Mahé
